text: Our dad died and left the house in his will. My sister A wants to buy it with her husband at a "family discount". I'm not signing off on that. Our younger sister B could use some money too. Can you help us sort this out?

Thank you for contacting me. I am sorry about your dad. I can help map concerns and look for a plan, but I cannot make legal decisions or move money. I have started one shared NCE list, where NCE means needs, concerns, and expectations, and I am sending the same first list to A, B, and C. First, C does not want to sign off on the proposed sale to A and her husband at a "family discount". Second, C says B could use money too, but B has not confirmed that. Third, C reports that A hopes to buy the house with her husband at that discount. Fourth, my own NCE is that I need a fair, clear process with all three sisters heard, no pressure to sign, and a shared record of concerns. Please correct anything I have got wrong, add your own NCEs, and say what you could accept. You can disagree with any item, including mine. If you know them, please share what the will says about the house, who is handling the estate, any deadlines, and whether the house has been valued.

Your list is mostly right. I haven’t agreed to A’s discounted purchase, and I won’t subsidize it; I want a fair financial share. I don’t know whether B needs money. I’d consider a purchase on fair, clearly established terms, with all three of us heard and no pressure to sign. I don’t know what the will says, who is handling the estate, or whether there’s a valuation or deadline. I’m not in a hurry.

I disagree with the only draft on the table as written: A and her husband buy now at a "family discount". It may serve your hope to buy the house, but it fails C's fair-share NCE, your own valuation and clear-terms NCE, B's inclusion NCE, and my checked-facts NCE. It also does not explain who gives up value. I am not rejecting your hope. I am saying we cannot judge it yet. A process draft could work better: pause signatures, get what the will says and the name of the person handling the estate, get a valuation from someone none of you chooses alone, then compare options with all three sisters heard. That process meets your valuation and clear-terms NCE, C's no-pressure NCE, B's inclusion NCE, and my checked-facts NCE. It leaves your purchase hope open. It does not yet set C's share or B's money, so I do not treat it as a final sale plan.
